subject: Follow-up: MedicAI privacy checklist & retention counteroffer
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena@medicai.com>, Tom Harris <tharris@medicai.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-28T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: MedicAI privacy checklist & retention counteroffer

Hi Elena / Tom —

Thanks again for the call earlier — great to get aligned on the high-level needs. Per our discussion I’m summarizing the key asks and our proposed path forward so we have a single place to iterate: 

- MedicAI asks:
  - PII/PHI: certain fields (name, SSN, patient identifiers) must not persist beyond request handling — effectively a 0-retention requirement for those token streams.
  - Logs: Retain inference logs for 7 days for debugging, but anonymize or truncate tokens that match patient identifiers.
  - Data residency: Primary storage in US region with contractual guarantee; some audit log copies requested for EU customers.
  - Evidence: SOC2 artifact and a short architecture doc showing isolation controls.

- Redwood proposed next steps:
  1) We can pilot a configuration that isolates MedicAI traffic to a dedicated pool and enables token-level masking for configured PII fields. This gives behavior equivalent to 0-retention for masked tokens while still allowing short-term telemetry for debugging.
  2) For logs we’ll propose a 7-day retention window with a reversible purge workflow (manual and automated) while providing anonymized summaries for metrics.
  3) Legal: Draft contract language for a data-retention carve-out + addendum for data residency. Marcus will lead that thread.
  4) Security: Rishi will collect the narrow set of artifacts you requested (SOC2 section pointers, key control descriptions).

Attachments: I’ve uploaded a working checklist to the shared Drive (link below) and attached MedicAI’s privacy checklist file you sent to this thread for reference.

Can you confirm the items above map correctly to what you need, and whether MedicAI can run a 4-week pilot on a dedicated pool (we’ll provide a short success criteria doc)? If yes, I’ll schedule a quick technical kick-off with Lauren and Rishi tomorrow.

Thanks,
Jonas
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Attachments: MedicAI-privacy-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet, 120KB)

From: Elena Ruiz <elena@medicai.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Harris <tharris@medicai.com>, privacy@medicai.com
Date: 2026-05-28T18:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: MedicAI privacy checklist & retention counteroffer

Jonas —

Thanks for the clear recap. That mostly aligns. A couple clarifications / constraints from our privacy team (copied):

1) "0-retention" expectation: For any request containing PHI (as defined in our attached checklist), we require that the raw token stream not be readable or restorable after processing. You said masking could achieve the same outcome — confirm that masked tokens will not be stored in any logs or backups in a way that could be reconstituted.

2) Logs window: 7 days is acceptable for debugging, but for PHI-bearing requests we want your system to automatically delete raw logs within 24 hours unless we explicitly opt-in for investigation.

3) Residency: Our legal will need the contractual guarantee that data will not leave US jurisdiction for our customers. We may later request EU residency for a subset of customers; can you confirm capabilities?

4) Evidence: Please provide the exact SOC2 sections that map to your logging / retention controls and the tweak list (what we should expect to see in an architecture diagram).

We attached an updated privacy checklist with bolded fields (MedicAI-privacy-checklist.xlsx) and a short redline to the contract language; not final, but it shows our starting point.

If Redwood can meet the 24-hour PHI log purge for PHI requests (and provide an auditable deletion event), we can move forward with a pilot next week. Otherwise we’ll need to escalate to procurement and legal for a longer review.

Elena Ruiz
Head of Privacy & Compliance | MedicAI
elena@medicai.com

Attachments: MedicAI-privacy-checklist.xlsx (updated), MedicAI-retention-redlines.docx

Hi Elena —

Quick technical note from my side after reviewing the checklist:

- Token-level masking: We can enable a pre-ingest filter that runs a PII/PHI detector and replaces the matching tokens with deterministic placeholders before any downstream KV caching or logs are written. In that mode the raw tokens never touch persistent storage; only the masked form does.

- Short-lived debug logs: Implementable as a separate, labeled log stream with a TTL. For PHI-bearing requests the TTL can be 24 hours and will be auto-purged; for non-PHI we can keep 7 days. Purge events are emitted to our audit stream (immutable) which contains only metadata (request id, timestamp, action) — not the raw tokens.

- Residency: Our hosted offering currently supports regionalized deployment in us-east-1 and eu-west-1. For the pilot we can provision a US-only pool and prevent cross-region failover. If you need an EU-copy later, we can discuss a geographically scoped deployment.

I attached a short architecture diagram that highlights where masking and purge hooks operate. For the pilot I’d suggest these success criteria:
  - PHI tokens masked before any persistent write (0-retention equivalence).
  - Automatic purge of PHI-labeled logs within 24 hours, with audit events emitted.
  - No cross-region replication for the tenant.

If those look good I’ll schedule a 30-min tech kickoff with your infra lead and a one-week pilot plan.

—Lauren
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai

Attachments: pilot-arch-diagram.png (PNG, 220KB)

Elena / team —

Thanks for the clarity and the redlines. I reviewed MedicAI’s requested language and sketched a balanced contractual approach that should satisfy both sides while keeping the deal executable. High-level proposal: 

1) PHI carve-out clause: Insert an addendum that defines "PHI-bearing requests" (by field/classification) and requires Redwood to implement token masking and to purge raw logs within 24 hours for those requests. Include a certified deletion event with a signed timestamp and request id.

2) Logs: Default debug log retention remains 7 days for non-PHI traffic. For PHI traffic, retention is capped at 24 hours as above.

3) Data residency: Contractual representation that MedicAI tenant data will be stored in the designated US region for the term of the agreement; any exceptional cross-region copies require written consent.

4) Audit & evidence: Rishi will provide SOC2 mapping and we can add an explicit right to request specific artifacts under an NDA for audit purposes.

I’m attaching a short draft (redwood-log-retention-draft.docx) with suggested language you can iterate on. If MedicAI accepts the high-level approach I propose we: (a) sign an MSA addendum for the pilot with these controls, (b) run the 4-week pilot described by Lauren, and (c) put the permanent language into the master services schedule pending successful pilot outcomes.

Happy to hop on a call if you want to walk the draft line-by-line. Jonas — can you propose times for the legal/technical review?

Marcus Lin
Deputy General Counsel | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-log-retention-draft.docx (draft language, 18KB)
